h1: Where to drink this weekend in Hyderabad: IPA
title: Hyderabad IPA this weekend | Craft Beer School
desc: Five Hyderabad breweries with an IPA on the list, from West Coast to hazy, what to eat with them and a Jubilee Hills plan for the evening.
teaser: A West Coast IPA in Jubilee Hills, a New England IPA in Madhapur. Here is where to taste the difference this weekend.
standfirst: Hyderabad's brewery lists cover both sides of IPA, clear and bitter as well as hazy and soft. Here are five places to try, three dishes to order and a plan that keeps the evening in one neighbourhood.
sections: IPA is the beer to taste side by side

American IPA took the English idea of a strong, well hopped pale ale and rebuilt it around American hops: Cascade, Centennial, Simcoe, Citra and their relatives. They smell of grapefruit, orange peel, pine and resin. Brewers add them in the kettle and again after fermentation, which is where most of that aroma comes from.

The classic version is gold to light amber and clear. Malt stays in the background, a little bread and light caramel, just enough to carry the hops. Bitterness is firm and the finish is dry. A good one smells like you have just cut a grapefruit open in a pine forest. A tired one smells of cardboard and onion, because hop aroma fades fast.

The West Coast version is the driest and most bitter. A hazy New England IPA sits at the other end. The clearest line between them is clarity and that bitter backbone. Ask for it at 6 to 9 °C in a tulip glass. Our American IPA style page has the full profile.
Five places to try one this weekend

These come from our brewery directory, which we last checked in September 2026. Taps rotate, so call ahead.

  • Zythum Brewing Co., Jubilee Hills. A West Coast IPA, the clear and bitter end of the style. Belgian Witbier and Czech Pilsner are on the same list.
  • The Hoppery, Jubilee Hills (KBR Park). The list simply says IPA. A Cinnamon Ale is the other one to ask about.
  • Vault Brewery, Jubilee Hills. Its IPA is NIPA, with a Bock and a House Wheat Beer alongside.
  • Red Rhino Craft Brewery, Madhapur / HITEC City. A New England IPA, plus an English Pale Ale and a Raspberry Pale Ale.
  • Red Rhino Taproom, Financial District. Also lists the New England IPA. Its status in our directory is unverified, so this is the one to ring first.

Put Zythum's West Coast IPA next to a New England IPA and the difference is obvious in the glass before you even smell it. Explaining it is harder. Why is one bitter and the other soft? Is that grassy note fresh hops or something gone wrong? A trained palate answers that in seconds. An untrained one shrugs.

Freshness matters as much as recipe. Hop aroma fades in weeks at room temperature, so an IPA poured at the brewery that made it is about as fresh as it gets in India. If one smells dull or papery rather than of grapefruit and pine, it is fair to ask how long the keg has been on.
Amritsari fish and galouti kebab are the safe picks

Bitterness amplifies chilli heat, so pick dishes with some care. These three work.

  • Amritsari fish. Citrus hops echo the ajwain and lemon. Bitterness cuts through the gram flour batter.
  • Mutton galouti kebab. Rich, smooth and melting. Here the beer works as a cut, not a cool: firm bitterness against all that richness.
  • Mushroom and onion uttapam. A mild, savoury plate that bread malt and grapefruit hops brighten up. Good for the vegetarian at the table.

Aged gouda is the wild card. It is easy to buy in Indian cities. The nutty, salty cheese softens the bitterness and draws the malt forward.
Jubilee Hills holds the whole evening

Zythum, The Hoppery and Vault are all in Jubilee Hills, so you can taste three IPAs without crossing the city. Pick two. Order a taster at each rather than a pint. Eat at the first stop. Finish on the West Coast IPA rather than start with it, because a strongly bitter beer makes whatever follows it taste flat.

Drink water between beers. Take a cab or the metro home. If anyone in your group is driving, they skip the beer: never drive after drinking.

Before you go, open the IPA style page and read the aroma notes. If the West Coast end of the style is the one that interests you, our West Coast IPA guide explains how brewers build it. For more dishes, see Indian food and beer pairing.
faqs: What is the difference between a West Coast IPA and a New England IPA?
A West Coast IPA is clear, dry and firmly bitter. A New England IPA is hazy and softer, with less bitterness and more juicy fruit.
What temperature should an IPA be served at?
Around 6 to 9 °C, in a tulip glass that holds the aroma.
Why does some IPA taste like cardboard?
Hop aroma fades quickly and stale beer picks up cardboard and onion notes. Fresh on tap at the brewery is the safest bet.
